sections.title: Form and habitat
sections.text: Chinese boxthorn is an erect or spreading shrub of East Asia, usually 0.5–1 m tall and reaching about 2 m in cultivation. It grows on slopes, disturbed ground and saline soils.

sections.title: Leaves, flowers and fruit
sections.text: The branches bear lateral spines 0.5–2 cm long. The leaves are about 1.5–5 cm long. The mauve flowers are about 1 cm across; red berries are usually 0.7–1.5 cm long.

sections.title: Edibility
sections.text: The ripe fruits are eaten; a Singapore botanical source also mentions the seeds. This entry does not specify a particular preparation or amount.
